reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Risk of a new AI divide
themes.definition: Concern that AI creates a new divide between those with skills and infrastructure to participate and those who only feel its effects; progress must not widen gaps.
themes.inclusion: Passages warning that AI could widen gaps between countries or societies with and without capacity.
themes.exclusion: Concrete skills or infrastructure programmes (use AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
themes.boundary_cases: Calls for all countries to benefit and contribute to AI rules take this and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: it also highlights the risk of a new divide between those who have the skills and infrastructure needed to participate in this transformation

themes.label: AI possibilities in science, medicine, education
themes.definition: AI presented as offering new possibilities in science, economy, medicine, education and resource management.
themes.inclusion: Passages listing AI's beneficial applications across sectors.
themes.exclusion: Mentions of benefits only as a list of technologies (use AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION).
themes.boundary_cases: When benefits are immediately paired with risks, also code AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY.

examples.quote: It offers considerable new possibilities in science, the economy, medicine, education, and the management of resources.

themes.label: Balancing innovation and trust in AI rules
themes.definition: AI governance framed as balancing innovation and public trust: rules should enable progress without stifling it while ensuring reliable, responsible development.
themes.inclusion: Passages arguing rules must neither block innovation nor allow untrusted innovation, e.g., 'Bridging Innovation and Trust'.
themes.exclusion: Calls for strict limits or bans without balance framing.
themes.boundary_cases: Hosting a summit on this balance counts here and in AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: Innovation in which societies no longer have confidence risks being rejected. Conversely, rules that would prevent all innovation would deprive us of enormous potential.

themes.label: Multilateral, inclusive AI rule-making
themes.definition: AI shows that no single state can manage its consequences; multilateral institutions and inclusive participation in AI rules are needed, e.g., via a Geneva AI Summit.
themes.inclusion: Passages calling for multilateral AI rules, inclusive participation in rule debates, or international summits on AI.
themes.exclusion: UN internal reform unrelated to AI.
themes.boundary_cases: Using AI as an argument for multilateralism generally still counts here.

examples.quote: no single state can manage all of their consequences by itself
contribute to the debate on the rules that will govern its development and use

value.rationale: Both Swiss passages treat AI as a cross-border transformation requiring inclusive multilateral governance, stressing a new divide, sectoral benefits and a balance between innovation and trust via the Geneva AI Summit.
